facts.statement: Emuarius was an extinct genus of flightless birds from Australia.
facts.quote: Emuarius is an extinct genus of casuariiform flightless bird from Australia

facts.statement: Birds in this genus are commonly called emuwaries.
facts.quote: The birds in this genus are known as emuwaries.

facts.statement: The name Emuarius combines the words 'emu' and 'cassowary'.
facts.quote: This name comes from a combination of emu and cassowary.

facts.statement: Emuarius had a skull and femur resembling a cassowary, but a lower leg and foot resembling an emu.
facts.quote: This is due to its cassowary-like skull and femur and emu-like lower leg and foot.

facts.statement: Emuarius gidju weighed an estimated 19 to 21 kilograms, which is less than a modern emu.
facts.quote: E. gidju has an estimated mass of 19-21 kg, less than the modern emu

facts.statement: Emuarius guljaruba is stated to be larger than Emuarius gidju.
facts.quote: E. guljaruba is stated to be larger than E. gidju.

facts.statement: The genus Emuarius was described in 1992 by Walter E. Boles.
facts.quote: El género Emuarius fue descrito en 1992 por Walter E. Boles

facts.statement: A second species named E. guljaruba was described in 2001.
facts.quote: En 2001 fue descrita una segunda especie que recibió el nombre de E. guljaruba.

facts.statement: The validity of the second species E. guljaruba has been questioned until more fossil material is discovered.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la validez de esta segunda especie ha sido puesta en duda hasta al menos el descubrimiento de más material fósil.

facts.statement: Emuarius lived in Australia during the late Oligocene and middle Miocene.
facts.quote: que vivió durante el Oligoceno superior y el Mioceno medio en Australia.

facts.statement: Emuarius is classified in the superorder Palaeognathae, order Casuariiformes, and family Casuariidae.
facts.quote: superordo: Palaeognathae ordo: Casuariiformes familia: Casuariidae

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis shows that Emuarius is a sister taxon to Dromaius.
facts.quote: Mediante análisis filogéneticos efectuados en la especie tipo, se ha demostrado que es un taxón hermano con Dromaius

facts.statement: Emuarius lived between 27.3 and 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Burdigalian (27.3 to 15.98 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Emuarius lived during the late Oligocene and early Miocene.
rejected.quote: It is one of two known genera of emu. It lived during the early Miocene and late Oligocene.
